title: Grover's Algorithm (2-Qubit Target |11⟩)
summary: Master Grover's search algorithm on 2 qubits to locate target state |11⟩ in a single quantum query with 100% probability via Oracle phase marking and Diffuser amplitude amplification.
learningObjectives: Prepare equal superposition across 4 basis states using Hadamard gates
Construct the Quantum Oracle to invert the phase of target state |11⟩
Understand why phase inversion alone leaves measurement probabilities unchanged at 25%
Construct the Grover Diffuser to reflect probability amplitudes about the mean
Observe constructive interference amplifying target |11⟩ to 100% probability in a single query
completionMessage: Congratulations! You mastered Grover's Search Algorithm on 2 qubits, verifying quadratic speedup O(√N) and 100% deterministic identification of target state |11⟩.

segments.title: 1. Ground State Initialization (|00⟩)
segments.explanation: We begin with two qubits initialized to the ground state |00⟩. In a 4-item unsorted database, our marked target item is |11⟩.
segments.narrationText: Welcome to the Grover's Algorithm live demonstration. In this masterclass, we search an unsorted four-item database to locate the marked target state 11. We begin with both qubits in the ground state 00.

segments.title: 2. Database Representation & Target State
segments.explanation: With 2 qubits, N = 2² = 4 possible database entries: |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, and target |11⟩. Classical search requires up to 4 queries; quantum search needs only 1 query.
segments.narrationText: Let's inspect the search space. Four possible entries exist: 00, 01, 10, and our marked target item 11. Classical search must test entries one by one, taking up to four checks. Grover's algorithm will isolate it in a single query.

actions.title: Search Space N = 4
actions.message: Unsorted entries: {|00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩}. Classical average: 2.25 queries; Grover quantum search: exactly 1 query.

segments.title: 3. Selecting Hadamard Gate
segments.explanation: To search all database items simultaneously, we must create an equal superposition across all basis states.
segments.narrationText: To evaluate all entries simultaneously, we must prepare an equal superposition. Watch the teaching cursor select the Hadamard gate from the operations palette.

segments.title: 4. Placing H Gate on Qubit 0
segments.explanation: Placing a Hadamard gate on qubit 0 puts it into superposition (|0⟩ + |1⟩)/√2.
segments.narrationText: First, we place a Hadamard gate on qubit zero, putting it into a superposition of zero and one.

segments.title: 5. Single Qubit Superposition
segments.explanation: Qubit 0 is now in equal superposition while qubit 1 remains in |0⟩, creating state (|00⟩ + |10⟩)/√2.
segments.narrationText: Qubit zero is now in superposition. Now let's do the same for qubit one to establish full two-qubit superposition.

segments.title: 6. Placing H Gate on Qubit 1
segments.explanation: Placing a Hadamard gate on qubit 1 completes the tensor product H ⊗ H, preparing equal superposition |s⟩.
segments.narrationText: We place a Hadamard gate on qubit one. Together, H tensored with H creates a uniform quantum superposition across all four computational basis states.

segments.title: 7. Equal Superposition State |s⟩
segments.explanation: State |s⟩ = 1/2 (|00⟩ + |01⟩ + |10⟩ + |11⟩). Every state has probability amplitude +1/2.
segments.narrationText: Notice the state formula on screen. All four basis states have an identical positive amplitude of one-half.

segments.title: 8. Uniform 25% Probability Distribution
segments.explanation: Because |1/2|² = 1/4 = 25%, each state has an equal 25% probability of being measured.
segments.narrationText: Looking at the probability panel, each of the four states has an equal twenty-five percent probability. At this stage, measuring the circuit would simply yield a random state.

segments.title: 9. Introducing the Quantum Oracle
segments.explanation: The Oracle U_ω recognizes the marked item and flips its phase: U_ω|x⟩ = -|x⟩ if x = ω, and +|x⟩ otherwise.
segments.narrationText: Now we introduce the Quantum Oracle. Instead of checking entries classically, the oracle marks our target item 11 by inverting its quantum phase.

segments.title: 10. Building the Oracle (Controlled-Z Gate)
segments.explanation: A Controlled-Z (CZ) gate acts as the exact Oracle for target |11⟩, applying a π phase shift exclusively to |11⟩.
segments.narrationText: Watch as we place a Controlled-Z gate across qubit zero and qubit one. This gate leaves states 00, 01, and 10 unchanged, but flips the sign of state 11.

segments.title: 11. Phase Marking: Inverting Target Amplitude
segments.explanation: The state is now: 1/2 (|00⟩ + |01⟩ + |10⟩ - |11⟩). Target |11⟩ has amplitude -1/2.
segments.narrationText: Target state 11 is now phase-marked. Its amplitude has flipped from positive one-half to negative one-half. However, because probability is the square of amplitude, its measurement probability is still twenty-five percent.

segments.title: 12. Q-Sphere Statevector Inspection
segments.explanation: On the Q-Sphere, observe how the state amplitudes have changed. Target |11⟩ now points in the opposite phase direction (180° / π phase).
segments.narrationText: Switching to the Q-Sphere visualization, notice how the state amplitudes have changed. The vector for target 11 has rotated to a negative phase, distinguished by its phase color shift.

segments.title: 13. Constructing the Grover Diffuser
segments.explanation: The Grover Diffuser D = 2|s⟩⟨s| - I is implemented via H, X, CZ, X, H gates. It inverts all amplitudes about their mean.
segments.narrationText: Now we construct the Grover Diffuser operator. Built from Hadamard, Pauli-X, and Controlled-Z gates, this operator performs an inversion about the mean, transforming phase differences into detectable amplitude differences.

segments.title: 14. Amplitude Amplification (Inversion About Mean)
segments.narrationText: Look closely at the mathematics. The average mean amplitude before reflection was one-fourth. Reflecting about the mean: two times one-fourth minus one-half gives zero for non-target states, while two times one-fourth minus negative one-half equals exactly one for target state 11!

segments.title: 15. Socratic Prediction: Final Measurement
segments.explanation: Before we simulate and measure the circuit, predict the physical measurement outcome based on amplitude amplification.
segments.narrationText: Before we run the quantum simulation and measure the circuit, test your understanding: what do you predict will happen when we measure the circuit?

checkpoint.question: What do you predict will happen when we measure the 2-qubit Grover circuit?

options.label: All 4 states will still be measured with equal 25% probability
options.description: Misconception: Diffuser does not change measurement statistics

options.label: Target state |11⟩ will be measured with 100% probability (0% for others)
options.description: Constructive interference amplifies target to amplitude 1.0

options.label: Target state |11⟩ cannot be measured because it has a negative probability
options.description: Misconception: Confusing negative phase with negative probability

checkpoint.explanation: Constructive interference boosts target |11⟩ amplitude to exactly 1.0 (|1.0|² = 100%), while destructive interference cancels out non-target states |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩ to 0!

segments.title: 16. Quantum Simulation Execution
segments.explanation: Executing quantum simulation across 1000 shots using the real simulation engine.
segments.narrationText: Now, let's execute the quantum simulation across one thousand shots to physically test our prediction.

segments.title: 17. Measurement Histogram: 100% Collapse
segments.explanation: All 1000 shots collapsed into target marked state |11⟩ with 100% probability. Non-target states have 0 counts.
segments.narrationText: Look at the measurement histogram! Every single one of the one thousand experimental trials collapsed into our target state 11. States 00, 01, and 10 have zero counts.

segments.title: 18. Interference Mechanism Explained
segments.explanation: Destructive interference cancelled out non-targets, while constructive interference amplified marked target |11⟩.
segments.narrationText: Through destructive interference, non-target states cancelled out completely. Constructive interference amplified target item 11 from twenty-five percent to one hundred percent in a single query.

actions.title: Quantum Speedup Verified
actions.message: Oracle phase inversion + Diffuser inversion about the mean converted a 25% uniform distribution into 100% deterministic isolation of target |11⟩ in 1 query.

segments.title: 19. Grover Algorithm Mastered
segments.explanation: Grover's Algorithm live demonstration completed! Quadratic quantum search speedup O(√N) successfully demonstrated.
segments.narrationText: Congratulations! You have completed the Grover Algorithm Masterclass. You have seen how superposition, phase marking, and amplitude amplification work together to achieve quadratic quantum search speedup.
